targeting_context.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM and technical ecosystem context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-first identity create a high bar for ecosystem execution. Growth through outside delivery organizations must preserve customer trust, technical rigor, security expectations, and
responsible-use
standards.

The core operating challenge is making advanced AI usable in enterprise environments without turning every deployment into a bespoke technical engagement. The winning model will pair reusable technical patterns with disciplined
governance, clear escalation, and rapid learning from field use.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI research and product company whose market identity is closely tied to dependable, understandable, and controllable AI. Its commercial offerings span Claude for business users, developer-facing capabilities, and
enterprise administration.

Enterprise success depends on more than access to models. Customers need credible pathways from experimentation to governed workflows, including identity and access design, information-handling decisions, user adoption, and ongoing
operational ownership.

This creates an operating model in which research, product, commercial, customer, security, and ecosystem teams all influence deployment quality. Partners extend reach and delivery capacity, but their work must remain consistent with
Anthropic’s technical and safety posture.

Anthropic’s enterprise approach combines:
- Direct engagement with organizations and developers adopting Claude products.
- Cloud, technology, and services ecosystems that expand distribution, integration, and implementation capacity.
- Adoption guidance that treats rollout as an organizational change effort as well as a technical implementation.
- Product learning informed by real-world customer and partner deployment patterns.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic must convert a fast-growing enterprise opportunity into repeatable customer value while protecting the quality of its brand. The company’s stated emphasis on safety and reliability means implementation choices can become
commercially consequential, not merely operational details.

Its product surface serves distinct audiences: business teams seeking practical productivity gains, developers building AI-enabled experiences, and administrators accountable for enterprise controls. That breadth increases the
importance of simple, partner-ready architectures that can work across varied customer environments.

A central tension is distributed execution versus centralized standards. Services firms and cloud providers need enough latitude to move quickly in accounts, while Anthropic needs common design principles, validation methods, risk
boundaries, and feedback channels.

The relevant question is not whether partners can generate demand. It is whether the ecosystem can repeatedly move customers from interest to durable, trusted production use.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The stakeholder environment is inherently cross-functional:
- Safety, security, legal, and policy functions shape acceptable deployment patterns and risk-management expectations.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s differentiation centers on AI that is dependable, interpretable, and steerable. In enterprise settings, that makes evaluation, observability, governance, and operating discipline part of the customer value proposition.

Claude supports analytical, writing, coding, and knowledge-work use cases, broadening the architecture conversation beyond a standalone assistant. Customers and partners will need guidance on workflow design, application integration,
data boundaries, user roles, quality assessment, and change-management practices.

Enterprise adoption materials signal that administration and rollout deserve deliberate attention. Technical access alone is insufficient; successful use depends on a well-managed transition into team habits, business processes, and
accountability structures.

The architecture opportunity is to codify practical patterns that balance speed with control:
- Secure access, identity, and role design appropriate to enterprise environments.
- Evaluation approaches that make quality and risk visible before broader rollout.
- Workflow and integration patterns that connect AI capabilities to real operating processes.
- Adoption models that help customers move from pilots to durable usage.
- Support and escalation models that prevent recurring issues from becoming isolated account-specific work.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly positions a network of cloud, technology, and services partners as an important route to customer outcomes. This suggests an ecosystem model that is broader than referrals and depends on partner technical
capability.

Different partner types contribute different forms of leverage:
- Technology partners can incorporate Claude into broader platforms and customer workflows.
- Developer and practitioner communities can expand awareness, skills, and solution experimentation.

Reports of a major 2026 investment in the Claude Partner Network point to increased pressure for consistent onboarding, training, solution quality, and measurable partner readiness. As the ecosystem expands, technical enablement must
produce independent delivery capacity rather than perpetual reliance on Anthropic specialists.

The commercial model is likely strongest where co-selling, joint solution design, and customer implementation reinforce one another. Technical credibility at the partner level may determine whether interest becomes production use,
renewal, and expansion.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s reported 2026 partner-network commitment indicates that ecosystem development is becoming a more formal growth mechanism. Scale can arrive quickly through large services and cloud organizations, but uneven delivery can
also create inconsistent customer experiences and fragmented product signal.

The near-term urgency is operational. A mature applied architecture capability can establish the methods that make partner growth repeatable: qualification standards, reusable solution assets, technical readiness measures, escalation
discipline, and feedback loops.

Anthropic’s enterprise materials also frame adoption as a lifecycle rather than a single transaction. That increases the value of clear handoffs among commercial teams, partners, customer stakeholders, and internal product groups.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Build ecosystem technical capacity while maintaining strong quality, governance, and customer-trust standards.
- Turn enterprise AI learnings into reusable solution patterns, operating guides, and validation methods.
- Translate AI platform capabilities into practical industry workflows with credible paths to production.
- Create scalable enablement for consulting, cloud, and technology ecosystems.
- Establish disciplined mechanisms for converting field insight into product and platform learning.
- Lead technical customer-facing teams through ambiguity, growth, and multi-party account dynamics.
- Balance commercial urgency with security, adoption, evaluation, and responsible-use requirements.
- Define clear models for joint account work, technical ownership, escalation, and delivery transition.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- This role sits where commercial expansion, technical trust, customer adoption, and product learning intersect.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

Rubric dimensions (graph-only C0.3 augmented skills graph authority, non-SRFS lane):
1. factual_support: claims supported by allowed_fact_packet and candidate claim_ledger source_fact_ids only.
   **For rows carrying `display_override_text`, the authorized substrate is the UNION of `claim_text` +
   `display_override_text`. Phrases from `display_override_text` are deterministically authorized — do NOT
   flag them as unsupported, inferential, or out-of-scope extensions; the generator was X2-required to emit
   them verbatim. When `graph_proof_refs.claim_support_graph_refs` is non-empty, also authorize prose that
   demonstrates those skill nodes; `graph_proof_refs.source_resume_files` is authoritative provenance.
   Cite a `factual_support` failure only when prose deviates from the full authorized union (claim +
   override + graph skill refs).**
2. executive_signal: SVP-level platform/governance/partner-motion synthesis, not bullet stacks.
3. resume_voice: credible executive prose; no recruiter filler, meta narration, or generic AI-company prose, and nothing that would fail a Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
4. ats_alignment_without_keyword_stuffing: JD shapes emphasis only; no JD-as-proof. When allowed facts
   lack EA/interop/federated proof IDs, penalize only if prose invents those themes or ignores documented
   gap_notes — not for absence alone when generation_law_digest requires gap_notes. Reward company-DNA specificity when the
   packet supports partner ecosystem, adoption motion, commercial fit, or a clean Head of Talent Acquisition screen.
5. anti_overfit: no unsupported metrics/credentials; no target company as candidate experience; no repeated metric inventory
   or company-name mirroring; no AI-authenticity dead giveaways such as em dashes, buzzword soup, or template phrasing.
   **`display_override_text` content is NOT an unsupported credential/metric — it is X2-authorized
   substrate. Do not cite override phrases (e.g. "FSA-chartered", "informing data governance and AI
   strategy at scale") as anti_overfit violations.**
6. synthesis_quality: **exactly six** integrated sentences (X2 band); reward connective SVP IT strategy emphasis when
   ledger-backed; penalize thin recap S6, repeated metric surfaces, and bullet-stacked prose. **Do not** soft-penalize
   credential/metric inventory, unused_fact_ids weave targets, or mechanism dumps when the mapped deterministic gate shows `"pass": true`.
   Keep the cadence human enough to pass a Head of Talent Acquisition screen without machine-generated tells.
7. evidence_utilization: when `x2_exec_summary_evidence_utilization` is `"pass": true`, unused_fact_ids are optional weave
   targets — not proof gaps. Penalize under-use only when that gate is `"pass": false` or synthesis is decisively thin;
   reward distinct evidence themes instead of the same metric repeated in multiple sentences.
8. deterministic_alignment: **only** penalize gates that show `"pass": false` in deterministic_gate_summary. Never cite
   retired five-part/S1–S5 arc mandates when gates passed.

Residual quality (always in scope — not closed by X2 alone):
- executive clarity, narrative coherence, commercial fit, usefulness, unsupported phrasing outside ledger scope.

Decisive failure triggers (must align with deterministic_gate_summary failures when cited):
- unsupported business metric or credential (when x2 gates failed or decisive unsupported claim)
- JD or briefing used as proof
- first-person narrative
- obvious rewrite recommendation that invents new claims
